## Summary

**DBcc** (Test, Decrement & Branch Conditional): Test failed? then Decrement Dn & conditional jump to label.

## Details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Operation | `If not cc then ( Dn – 1 → Dn ; if Dn <> – 1 then PC + dn → PC )` |
| Syntax | `DBcc.L Dn,<label>` |
| Short | Test failed? then Decrement Dn & conditional jump to label. |
| Description | Controls a loop of instructions. If condition is true the loop ends and the program continues with the next instruction. Else Dn is decremented by 1. If Dn = – 1 the loop also ends and the program continues with the next instruction. If Dn &lt;&gt; – 1 the loop continues and the program execution continues at location (PC) + displacement. The displacement is always even. When it appears as odd, then the counter is a long, not a word. Read the displacement as if that bit is zero. |
| Condition codes | not affected |

### Encoding

| Word | Bits | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 15–12 | `0101` |
| 1 | 11–8 | Condition |
| 1 | 7–3 | `11001` |
| 1 | 2–0 | Register |
| 2 | 15–1 | 16 bit Displacement |
| 2 | 0 | `1` |

### Notes

- Variant on DBcc (that uses a word size counter)
- This long version uses 32bits to count.
- dbra is accepted by most assemblers for dbf. With dbf no condition is tested, only a count terminates the loop. This crippled unofficial version is ironically about the only one used of the group.
- Bank prefix needs to set the destination operand B.

## Differences from AmigaOS / AROS / 68060

- The 68000–68060 have DBcc. This page covers only the 68080 addition: DBcc.L with a 32-bit loop counter. For the classic forms, the Motorola manual applies.

## Do / Don't

- No rules beyond the details above.
